results.reader_title: A fuzzy Delphi method for judging immature technologies
results.reader_what: Authors build a stepwise expert-based method to evaluate early-stage technologies, tested on electric-vehicle battery disassembly.
results.reader_why: Gives analysts a reproducible way to rank technologies when hard data are scarce.
results.reader_more: The method combines systematic stakeholder mapping, 65 expert interviews producing 16 criteria, Delphi weighting of criteria, and a fuzzy Delphi panel scoring technologies. Fuzzy Delphi lets experts express uncertain judgements as ranges. In the case study, laser cutting and shredding scored best. The authors claim the process transfers to other technology domains under certain conditions.

deep_analysis.research_question: How can early-stage emerging technologies be evaluated systematically under high uncertainty?
deep_analysis.main_finding: A fuzzy Delphi-based multi-stage procedure yields transparent technology rankings; laser cutting and shredding rank highest for battery disassembly.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Stakeholder analysis, 65 interviews, two Delphi panels (13 experts) with fuzzy Delphi consensus rounds.
deep_analysis.qualification: Validated on a single use case; expert panel composition limits generalisability.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Reusable technology-assessment method for foresight and R&I prioritisation (Strand B).
